attrs.question: What are the security trade-offs between passkeys and SMS codes for bank logins?

attrs.sub_question: What attacks are SMS one-time codes vulnerable to in bank login flows (SIM swapping, SS7 interception, phishing/real-time relay, malware, number porting), and how resistant are passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn) to those same attacks, based on documented incidents, regulator guidance (e.g., NIST SP 800-63B, FFIEC, PSD2/EBA SCA) and bank deployment reports?

What attacks are SMS one-time codes vulnerable to in bank login flows (SIM swapping, SS7 interception, phishing/real-time relay, malware, number porting), and how resistant are passkeys (FIDO2/WebAuthn) to those same attacks, based on documented incidents, regulator guidance (e.g., NIST SP 800-63B, FFIEC, PSD2/EBA SCA) and bank deployment reports?

What are the security risks, limitations and weaknesses of passkeys for bank logins, including account recovery and fallback paths (often reverting to SMS), synced-passkey cloud account compromise, device theft or loss, shared devices, platform lock-in, and accessibility or adoption gaps, and where does SMS retain practical advantages?
